title: Example 286 mutant-security through the adapter entry: the frozen decision claim on the constructed mutant of 5.3.19, expected refuted
description: The frozen claim claims/disallowed-field-denied-ignoring-case.json, unchanged, run by examples/286-spring-framework-cve-2022-22968-case-sensitive-disallowed-fields/proofs/prove.py: jvmcontract prove (own checker, strict gaps) of example286.adapter.BinderDecisionAdapter#allowed(String[] allowedPatterns, String[] disallowedPatterns, String field), the entry the claim's first assumption names, with the claim's assumption, assertion and nullable parameters as they are written (streams, lambdas and java.util.regex, compiled by javac and run as bytecode) and the lemma examples/286-spring-framework-cve-2022-22968-case-sensitive-disallowed-fields/proofs/simple-match.contract (PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch on ASCII Strings is the claim's regular expression, proved first by induction on the pattern's length and applied where it was proved). The class path is the revision's pinned JARs, each checked against its SHA-256, and the adapter compiled against them. This is a proof beside the example route, whose own attempt of the task stops at DataBinder's receiver (VF-027): the route runs the verifier on the original artifact alone and has no adapter entry. Until this change jvmcontract refused the claim at its String[] parameters, its expressions and every String, StringBuilder, stream and regex call on the way. Here on the constructed mutant (fixed-release with controls/pattern-side-unnormalized.patch: the patterns are no longer lower-cased, the field still is), expected refuted, at the frozen bound of 8. prove.py builds the mutant as sources.lock.json says: DataBinder.java from the 5.3.19 sources JAR (SHA-256 and git blob checked), patched (patch and patched blob checked), compiled with --release 8 and put in a copy of the spring-context JAR in place of the class. Inline at 3 code units the claim was refuted in 6 s at allowed(allowedPatterns=null, disallowedPatterns={null, "[%]", "T**"}, field="T"), an exact-case match the mutant no longer denies, as mutant-replay's probes predicted; the witness is run in the harness on a JVM.
expected: exits 0: prove.py prints 'verdict: violation (expected violation)', the witness 'run on a JVM'

resources.notes: as the vulnerable-security job: a refutation, after the lemma's proof.
